written_after: tournament Phase-3 verdict: no credible candidate; greedy remains best empirically supported among evaluated candidates
metric: realized MSMI/100, paired on identical worlds, cluster-by-seed CI

methods.mechanism: On dev-only seeds (90210 family x 6 variants), run greedy episodes with a decision-day dump: feasible edges + scores, chosen pairs, compatible-but-unmatched members, ask spend, availability/busy windows; join each historical introduction with feedback events observed within a fixed horizon to label conversions. Produce feature x conversion-rate tables using ONLY decision-time-visible fields (fields/field_status, wait days, feasible degree, past feedback, ask_log).
methods.expected_benefit: Locates and quantifies where greedy actually loses (conversion heterogeneity, unserved-member patterns, blocking), converting 'try another idea' into measured loss channels; decides which of n02/n03/n04 deserve implementation. May show the binding constraint is field observation rather than pairing.
methods.implementation_effort: S-M (~1-2 days): reuses evaluate.episode in-process like instrument.py; kit/frozen files untouched; output = analysis artifacts only
methods.failure_mode: No legal decision-time feature separates conversion outcomes, or effects are <5% of introductions -> the feedback/stateful families have no signal and must not be built (this is a cheap, successful kill).
evidence_needed_to_justify_followons: >=1 decision-time-legal feature with conversion-rate ratio >= 2x between halves
that split covers >= 5% of introductions on >= 3 of 6 variants
replicates on >= 3 dev seeds (not a single-seed artifact)
additionally for P4 only: >= 5% of matched pairs are low-prospect while both endpoints had a better-compatible arrival inside the busy window (thick variants), with rate ~ 0 on cold_start/delayed

methods.mechanism: Keep greedy's structure (score -> greedy take) but reweight pair scores by conversion history already visible at decision time: smooth empirical conversion rates of pair types (agreement patterns on SOFT/REL fields) built from state['feedback'] + state['introductions']; blend with base score; when history < N events, output is byte-identical to control (guard). Ask phase = baseline_asks (isolates the match lever).
methods.expected_benefit: Targets the metric's real leverage (which pairs date -> conversions), the one lesson from m14/m26 no-ops: only changed conversions move MSMI. Bounded downside: guard makes worst case = control.
methods.implementation_effort: S-M (decide fn + smoothing constants + TDD fixtures incl. thin-history guard and determinism; ~1 day)
methods.failure_mode: Feedback too sparse early (cold_start) -> guard keeps it = control (no gain, no loss); rates non-stationary across variants -> smoothing window mis-set; looks identical to family A if blending weight is too low (must differ measurably: distinct digests on thick variants).
evidence_needed_to_justify_testing: P1 gate met (all three replication conditions)
offline backtest on P1 dumps: reweighting selects a converting pair where greedy selected a non-converting one on >= 3% of decision days that have edges
no cold_start regression in backtest (guard verified to bind)

methods.mechanism: Choose next-day SOFT asks from what history shows converts: build rolling per-field-option response/conversion stats from state['ask_log'] + state['feedback'] (both already in observe()); prioritize fields whose observed answers historically preceded mutual interest for similar members; keep the constraints-bundle-first rule; carry compact rolling counters in protocol memory only if recomputation is too costly (note: state already contains full history, so memory is convenience, not capability - evaluate.py L32 caps its size).
methods.expected_benefit: Untested half of asking: m29/m30 were static rules and failed; history-conditioned allocation could raise conversion per introduction (instrument shows mutual/intro ~0.15 and MSMI/intro near 0 on the sample seed - conversions are the scarce output).
methods.implementation_effort: M (~2-3 days): ask logic + rolling-stat builder + memory size tests + protocol roundtrip fixtures
methods.failure_mode: Same cold_start sparsity as n02 (needs guard -> baseline_asks until enough ask_log history); memory cap exceeded would create invalid episodes (must be unit-tested up front); ask budget reallocation could reduce coverage (guardrail: coverage delta >= -0.05).
evidence_needed_to_justify_testing: P1 gate met, AND P1 dumps show ask outcomes are decision-time predictable: fields chosen by baseline_asks convert at measurably different rates than unchosen observed fields (ratio >= 1.5x on >= 3 variants)
ask_log history is non-trivial: >= 30 logged ask answers before day 40 on >= 4 variants (else no learning material)

methods.mechanism: For each candidate pair, compare match-now value against preserved value: estimate each endpoint's future partner quality from the arrival stream observed so far (distribution of new arrivals' observed fields + endpoint's current feasible-degree trend) and the pair's conversion probability (from P1/n02 stats). Drop a match only when BOTH endpoints' expected future partners exceed the current pair AND conversion probability is low. HARD GUARD: never wait when today's edge count <= T_thin or either endpoint's wait exceeds a cap (reproduces the exact failure condition of families m16-m23 so it cannot repeat it).
methods.expected_benefit: Family C failed only because waiting was unconditional; conditional value-based waiting on thick markets could pair high-compatibility members with better future matches while the guard protects scarce markets. Coverage ~0.32 and ~33% zero-selection days show service headroom.
methods.implementation_effort: M-L (~4-6 days incl. arrival-rate estimator and backtest harness; gated behind P1)
methods.failure_mode: Estimator noise drops converting pairs (the proven losing move - every dropped pair is a lost date); guard mis-set re-fails cold_start/delayed exactly like m16/m18/m21/m22/m25; latency must stay << 10 s/invoke (budget check: current worst 0.43 s/invoke).
evidence_needed_to_justify_testing: P1 'blocking' condition met (>= 5% low-prospect matches with better-compatible arrival inside busy window, ~0 on cold_start/delayed)
offline replay on P1 dumps: guarded rule keeps 100% of greedy's converting pairs on cold_start/delayed and strictly improves conversion on >= 4 of 6 variants
estimated per-invoke cost <= 2 s (stay under the 10 s/invoke gate with margin)

explicitly_not_proposed: any variant of families A-E with new formulas or thresholds (ruled out by evidence)
re-running or re-tuning any of m01-m30 (frozen; results preserved)
comparing absolute scores across screening/confirm1/confirm2 seed sets
claiming greedy is globally optimal (only 'best empirically supported among evaluated')
